name: orb_pullback_entry_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Instead of entering at the ORB breakout level (standard approach), waiting for a pullback to the ORB_high (for longs) or ORB_low (for shorts) after the initial breakout provides a better entry price and higher win rate. The pullback entry works because: (1) it confirms the ORB level as support/resistance (role reversal), (2) it eliminates many false breakouts (which don't pull back — they just fail), and (3) it provides a tighter stop (just below the ORB level) vs breakout entry (which uses ORB_mid as stop). The tradeoff is missing fast breakouts that never pull back (~30% of successful breakouts). The inefficiency exists because breakout traders have FOMO and enter immediately rather than waiting for the pullback.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; ORB breakout confirmed then pullback to ORB level
indicators: breakout_confirmed = close was > ORB_high_15 (or < ORB_low_15) for 3+ bars
pullback_to_ORB = close within 0.05% of ORB_high_15 (long) or ORB_low_15 (short)
pullback_bar_count = bars between breakout and pullback
support_test = low touches ORB_high_15 ± 0.05% but close stays above (long)

conditions: breakout_confirmed == True (price broke above ORB_high for 3+ bars)
pullback_to_ORB == True (price has pulled back to ORB_high level)
long.confirmation: bounce bar closes above ORB_high_15 with rising volume (buyers defending level)

conditions: breakout_confirmed for shorts (close < ORB_low_15 for 3+ bars)
pullback_to_ORB == True (price pulled back up to ORB_low level)
resistance_test: high touches ORB_low_15 ± 0.05% but close stays below
short.confirmation: rejection bar closes below ORB_low_15 with rising volume (sellers defending level)

entry.entry_price: limit order at ORB_high_15 (long) or ORB_low_15 (short) — precise level entry

exit.target: 2.0 * ORB_range_15 from ORB_high/low (same target as standard ORB, but better entry = better RR)
exit.stop_loss: 0.3 * ORB_range_15 below ORB_high (long) or above ORB_low (short) — tight stop just below the level
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.0 * ORB_range_15, trail at ORB_high/low (the level that held as support/resistance)
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 150 mins without 50% target
exit.signal_exit: if close breaks below ORB_high by > 0.1% (support broken), exit immediately

risk.position_sizing: risk-based: shares = capital * 0.003 / (0.3 * ORB_range_15) — tighter stop allows larger size

filters.time_filter: pullback entry between 09:35-11:00 IST; pullbacks later in the day are less reliable
filters.trend_filter: ORB breakout direction aligned with NIFTY direction preferred
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has earnings; skip F&O expiry
other_filters: pullback must occur within 30 bars of breakout; longer pullbacks suggest weak momentum, not true retest

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — pullback entry is a well-known concept but requires patience that most traders lack

weaknesses: ~30% of successful ORB breakouts never pull back to the ORB level — they extend immediately, and this strategy misses them entirely
The pullback entry can trigger on what's actually a failed breakout that's reverting through the ORB range; the 'support test' can be a bear trap
Limit order at ORB level may not fill exactly due to rapid price movement; partial fills and slippage at the exact level are common
prior_art: Brooks (2009) pullback entries; Bulkowski (2005) on throwback/pullback patterns. Markman (2003) 'Swing Trading' pullback concepts applied to ORB.
notes: Edge math: 0.62 * 55bps - 0.38 * 15bps = 34.1 - 5.7 = 28.4bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~19.4bps/trade * 1 trade = ~19.4bps daily. The tight stop (0.3 * ORB_range vs 0.5 * ORB_range for standard) is the key advantage — it creates 2.28 profit factor vs ~1.7 for standard ORB. The tradeoff is lower frequency.
